Customer VOC:I am writing to lodge a formal complaint against two NEXA authorised service centres for deficient service and unfair denial of a clear defect that arose directly from a clutch assembly replacement carried out by your network. Vehicle Details: Make & Model: Maruti Suzuki Jimny (5-door, Indian version) Registration Number: UP53ER 1335 Chasis Number: MA3JJC7AWPE130866 Brief Facts of the Case: Due to a family medical emergency in Lucknow, I had to get my vehicle repaired at Mega Motors, Gomti Nagar, Lucknow (NEXA authorised workshop). The vehicle had a burned clutch assembly. I was quoted approximately ₹15,000 for the full clutch plate assembly replacement. I authorised the job and the vehicle was handed over for repair. Because of the ongoing medical emergency, I could not personally collect the vehicle. I arranged for my driver to pick it up from the Lucknow workshop after they confirmed that the repair was complete and the vehicle was ready. My driver drove the vehicle back to Gorakhpur. The very next day when I personally drove the vehicle, I noticed a distinct crackling / rattling noise that appears at speeds above 40–50 km/h, specifically in 4th and 5th gear. I immediately took the vehicle to the authorised NEXA Service Centre at Bhagat Chauraha, Taramandal Road, Budh Vihar Colony, Gorakhpur. They retained the vehicle for five full days.During this period, the Gorakhpur workshop gave contradictory statements: Initially they claimed that the gearbox is damaged and needs replacement. Later they changed their position and said the gearbox is functioning normally. Finally, they outright denied the existence of any problem, stating they “cannot locate the source of the noise”. Important Technical Observation:The noise completely disappears the moment the clutch pedal is pressed. This is a classic and well-documented symptom of an issue with the pilot bearing (spigot bearing) or input shaft bearing — components that are directly handled and should have been properly inspected/replaced during any clutch assembly replacement job.
The fact that this noise appeared immediately after the clutch replacement performed at your authorised Lucknow workshop, and is easily reproducible, clearly establishes that the defect is a direct consequence of deficient workmanship during the said repair.
My Grievance:Despite the vehicle being under the warranty of the recent authorised repair, the Gorakhpur NEXA centre is refusing to diagnose and rectify the issue properly. This amounts to:Deficiency in serviceCausing me significant mental agony, inconvenience, and potential risk of further damage My Demands: Immediate registration of this complaint and allocation of a formal Interaction / Complaint ID. Direction to both the Lucknow (Mega Motors) and Gorakhpur NEXA workshops to jointly diagnose the issue properly (including road test with video evidence) and carry out necessary repair/replacement of the pilot bearing and/or input shaft bearing (or any other related components) free of cost under the warranty of the previous clutch repair job. Reasonable compensation for the mental harassment, inconvenience, loss of time, and any actual expenses incurred (driver charges, extra travel, etc.). Written confirmation of the action taken within 7 working days of receipt of this complaint. Personal Mobile Number=7992184140 Documents Attached=job card of mega motors,registration paper of vehicle,receipt of the repair.=============synopsis========================Customer concern regarding a deficient after-sales service and denial of a genuine post-repair defect involving a Maruti Suzuki Jimny (UP53ER 1335). Following a clutch assembly replacement costing approximately ₹15,000 at Mega Motors (NEXA Gomti Nagar, Lucknow), a distinct crackling and rattling noise emerged at speeds above 40–50 km/h in 4th and 5th gear, which disappears entirely when the clutch pedal is pressed. Despite the issue being an evident symptom of a faulty pilot or input shaft bearing handled during the initial repair, the NEXA service centre at Bhagat Chauraha, Gorakhpur, held the vehicle for five days, issued contradictory statements, and ultimately refused free rectification under the previous repair warranty. The customer demands immediate corporate intervention, a joint diagnosis by both workshops, free repairs, and compensation for mental harassment. Kindly look into this matter.

VOC: At this stage, I am compelled to say that this matter is no longer only about a vehicle.

It is about trust, honesty, accountability and the treatment being given to a customer after accepting nearly ₹20 lakh of his hard-earned money.

I did not pay using invalid currency notes.

I did not pay using torn notes.

I paid every rupee through valid, hard-earned money believing that I was purchasing a premium NEXA vehicle backed by the trust and reputation of Maruti Suzuki.

In return, what have I received?

For months, I have received nothing except repeated denials, repeated demands for evidence, repeated delays and repeated attempts to avoid the real issue.

From Day One:

• I have maintained that no accident ever occurred while the vehicle was in my possession.

• I have consistently stated that no bonnet repair or repainting was ever carried out by me.

• I have continuously submitted photographs, videos, recordings, screenshots, travel records and technical observations.

• I have repeatedly offered to provide affidavits, declarations and any technical verification required.

• I have repeatedly requested independent inspections and technical verification.

Yet from Day One, the dealership has refused to positively engage with any independent verification process.

From Day One, every suggestion was met with excuses.

From Day One, every piece of evidence submitted by me was questioned.

From Day One, every observation made by me was dismissed.

From Day One, the only response I have received is:

"The vehicle was non-accidental."

"Your representative inspected it."

"PDI was done."

The recent inspection findings now officially confirm that the bonnet is not in OEM paint condition and has undergone repainting/repair work outside the OEM manufacturing process.

This is not my statement.

This is not an assumption.

This is not a theory.

This is the conclusion arising from the inspection and paint thickness analysis itself.

Even after this, the dealership continues to avoid answering the most important question:

If the bonnet has undergone repainting or repair work, then when, where and by whom was that work carried out?

I have already stated under full responsibility that it was not carried out during my ownership.

I am prepared even today to provide this statement through affidavit, notarized declaration or any legally binding document.

Another fact that has become even more significant is that the Grand Vitara hood emblem presently fitted on the bonnet is the same emblem that was installed when the vehicle was delivered from Lucknow.

Photographic evidence of the vehicle from the time of delivery already exists.

This fact raises serious questions regarding the chronology of events and deserves proper investigation.

Further, my representative had raised concerns regarding visible dots, paint irregularities and unusual surface appearance on the bonnet at the time of delivery itself.

These concerns were communicated immediately.

Instead of investigating the matter, assurances were given that the vehicle was 100% non-accidental and everything was normal.

Trusting those assurances, I accepted delivery.

Today, after months of correspondence, those concerns appear far more relevant than they were made out to be at that time.

What disappoints me most is not merely the condition of the vehicle.

What disappoints me is the complete lack of willingness shown towards finding the truth.

Not a single meaningful effort was made to independently verify my concerns until repeated escalations forced the matter forward.

Not a single proactive call was received offering a genuine solution.

Almost every communication, follow-up and effort has come from my side.

I have spent countless hours on emails, phone calls, inspections, visits and explanations.

I have suffered mental stress, professional embarrassment and loss of confidence in a brand that I genuinely trusted.

As a person involved in the automobile business myself, this issue has affected my credibility as well.

Customers naturally ask me:

"If this can happen to a person who himself deals in vehicles, what protection do ordinary customers have?"

That is the damage that cannot be measured in rupees.

The issue before us is simple.

I paid for a new, non-accidental vehicle.

I expect a new, non-accidental vehicle.

I did not agree to purchase a vehicle that would later be found to have a bonnet that is not in OEM paint condition.

Therefore, I once again request a fair resolution.

Either provide me with the product for which I paid, or provide an appropriate remedy consistent with the facts that have now emerged through inspection and technical analysis.

I have cooperated throughout this process.

I have provided evidence throughout this process.

I have remained patient throughout this process.

The time has now come for accountability and resolution.===================================================================================================================Synopsis: The customer, a professional in the automobile business, is seeking a fair resolution or product replacement from Maruti Suzuki (Nexa) after discovering through recent technical inspection and paint thickness analysis that the bonnet of his newly purchased Grand Vitara (valued at nearly ₹20 lakh) is not in OEM paint condition and has undergone prior repainting and repair work. Despite raising concerns about paint irregularities at the time of delivery in Lucknow—which were dismissed by the dealership with assurances that the car was entirely non-accidental—the customer has faced months of repeated denials, delays, and a total lack of accountability from the brand. Maintaining under full legal responsibility that no accident or repair occurred during his ownership, the customer highlights that the delivery-day hood emblem remains unchanged, proving the defect existed pre-delivery. He emphasizes that the dealership’s defensive posture has caused him significant mental stress, professional embarrassment, and damage to his business credibility, and he demands that the company finally acknowledge the inspection findings and deliver the pristine, non-accidental vehicle he rightfully paid for. Kindly look into the concern

Dear Sir/Madam,

I am writing to seek your intervention regarding my extremely disappointing experience with my new Maruti Suzuki Baleno purchased from Autopace Network Pvt. Ltd. (Nexa), Chandigarh on 3 April 2026.

On 23 April 2026, we submitted all required documents, including my friend's valid driving licence, and left the vehicle at the workshop for insurance processing. The next day, dealership staff informed us that the claim could not proceed because the driver was not a blood relative and advised us to wait until I obtained my permanent driving licence.

I am deeply concerned that the dealership's advice may have directly contributed to the rejection of my claim. Had correct guidance been provided initially, the claim could have been processed on the basis of the valid driving licence already submitted.

Additionally, I was informed during the claim process that the repair cost was approximately ₹35,000. However, after claim rejection, I was quoted approximately ₹17,000 for the same repairs if paid personally. This significant difference raises serious concerns regarding transparency and fairness.

I am also disappointed by the unprofessional behaviour, repeated arguments, and pressure from dealership staff to provide a 10-star rating despite unresolved issues.

IFFCO Tokio Insurance was strongly recommended to us with assurances of a smooth claim process. Unfortunately, the overall experience has been exactly the opposite.

I possess supporting evidence including service records, job cards, repair estimates, claim-related documents, photographs, chats, and other communications.

I respectfully request:

1. Investigation into the conduct of Autopace Network Pvt. Ltd., Chandigarh.
2. Written clarification regarding the alleged "blood relation" requirement.
3. Review of the insurance claim rejection.
4. Clarification regarding the difference between the ₹35,000 and ₹17,000 repair estimates.
5. Appropriate action regarding the misleading guidance provided.
6. Compensation for the inconvenience, time, and financial loss suffered.

Maruti Suzuki India Limited promotes and sells its vehicles on the strength of its nationwide service network and after-sales support. Customers reasonably expect that critical components required for repair will be made available within a reasonable period. The purpose of this communication is to place on record the sequence of events that has resulted in a complete loss of trust and confidence in your dealership. Your sales representative, Mr. Ragu (Mobile No. 9632778093), repeatedly assured us that the Maruti Suzuki Brezza booked by us would be delivered on 02 June 2026. Based on this assurance and at the insistence of your dealership, we made the full payment for the vehicle on 29 May 2026. After receiving the entire payment, your dealership failed to deliver the vehicle on the committed date. More importantly, there was no proactive communication from your team regarding the status of the vehicle. At every stage, we had to repeatedly follow up and seek updates ourselves. Not a single update was voluntarily shared by your team despite having received the full vehicle consideration amount. On the night of 31 May 2026, just before the scheduled delivery, we were informed by Mr. Ragu that the vehicle intended for us had developed a technical issue and could not be delivered. We were further informed that another vehicle had to be arranged and that delivery would be delayed by approximately fifteen days. Although this development was highly disappointing, we accepted the explanation in good faith and agreed to wait for the revised delivery schedule. Thereafter, we were informed that the vehicle would be delivered on 18 June 2026. However, when my wife contacted Mr. Ragu on 17 June 2026 to understand the delivery timing and make necessary arrangements, she was informed that the vehicle would not be delivered on 18 June 2026 and that delivery would only happen sometime next week. This information was again communicated only after we initiated the follow-up. The most disturbing aspect of this entire experience has been the behaviour displayed by your representative. Instead of showing empathy and professionalism after repeated delays, my wife was spoken to in a rude, dismissive and disrespectful manner. The interaction reflected a complete lack of customer sensitivity and professionalism expected from an authorized Maruti Suzuki dealership. Further, when we requested details of senior management to escalate the issue, Mr. Ragu responded in an arrogant and unprofessional manner, stating that despite working with the company for more than five years, he neither knew nor could provide details of the Managing Director. Such conduct is unacceptable and reflects poorly on the culture and customer service standards of your dealership We are also unable to understand why: • Full payment was collected on 29 May 2026. • Invoice was generated only on 06 June 2026. • Invoice was shared only after repeated follow-ups from our side. • Delivery commitments were repeatedly changed without any written communication. At this stage, the issue is no longer about a delayed vehicle delivery. The repeated broken commitments, lack of transparency, poor communication, absence of ownership, and unacceptable behaviour of your staff have completely eroded our confidence in proceeding with the purchase through your dealership. Accordingly, we hereby request: Immediate cancellation of the vehicle booking. Refund of the entire amount paid by us without any deductions. Payment of interest on the amount retained by your dealership from 29 May 2026 until the date of actual refund. Written confirmation of the cancellation and refund timeline. An explanation regarding the delay in invoicing and repeated failure to honour delivery commitments. Investigation into the conduct of the concerned employee and suitable corrective action. Please treat this matter as urgent and provide written confirmation of the refund process within 48 hours of receipt of this email. In the event of non-resolution, we reserve our right to pursue the matter before Maruti Suzuki India Limited, Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission and other appropriate legal forums for recovery of our funds, interest, compensation for mental harassment and all other remedies available under law. We hope you will resolve this matter professionally and without further delay. --------- synopsis --------- Customer is extremely dissatisfied with Bimal Auto Agency regarding the purchase of a Maruti Suzuki Brezza. Despite making the full payment on 29 May 2026 based on a delivery promise of 02 June 2026, the dealership repeatedly failed to deliver the car, delayed the invoice generation until 06 June 2026, and shifted timelines multiple times without proactive communication. Furthermore, sales representative Mr. Ragu (9632778093) spoke to the customer’s wife in a rude, dismissive, and arrogant manner, while refusing to share senior management contact details. Due to broken commitments, total lack of transparency, and unprofessional staff behavior, the customer has lost all trust and demands immediate booking cancellation, a full refund of the paid amount with interest within 48 hours, and strict disciplinary action against the employee. Kindly look into this matter and provide the update to the customer.

After independent inspection, the vehicle shows clear signs of repainting/bodywork, including visible spray/paint marks on the glass.

I have also received different explanations at different times, including rear-door scratches, rear-door damage, minor roof damage, and now sign-board impact on the roof. Therefore, I request a complete written clarification supported by records.

1. Complete PDI report with date, odometer reading, checklist, and inspector details.
2. Delivery checklist/customer delivery note with odometer reading.
3. Stockyard inward inspection report.

9. Complete DMS/service/job-card history against the VIN/chassis number from vehicle arrival till delivery.
10. Written explanation why no proper job card was created/provided for the painting/repainting/bodywork.
11. Written clarification regarding the unsigned stamp-paper undertaking mentioning 300 km running and scratches.
12. Written confirmation whether roof panel, pillars, glass, doors, hinges, chassis/frame, suspension, engine, gearbox, transfer case, differential, or electrical systems were affected.

इस मामले को प्राथमिकता के आधार पर लेते हुए संबंधित विभाग को तुरंत थर्मल रिपोर्ट जारी करने के निर्देश दें।
